title: Coordinate supported products and recursive closed adjoints
statement:
Fix the finite datum of [def-pur-conventions]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, $n\geq1$, and $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. All bases below are separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Use the specified pro-etale Tate twists [def-coefficient-twists-detailed], constructible exceptional inverse image [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], and adjunction-preserving composition comparisons [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction, def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate].

Let $B$ be such a base, $X_r=\mathbf A^r_B$, $p_r:X_r\to B$, $z_r:B\hookrightarrow X_r$, $q_r:X_{r+1}\to X_r$ the last-coordinate projection and $s_r:X_r\hookrightarrow X_{r+1}$ its zero section [def-sbc-affine-space], and put $W_r=A_{X_r}(r)[2r]$. For $c\geq0$, let $C_c:z_{c*}A_B\to W_c$ be the ordered product of coordinate Cartier-Kummer morphisms [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map, def-pur-affine-space-coordinate-boundaries], using [def-pur-supported-cup] and the canonical transport of their scheme-theoretic total intersection to $B$ [def-pur-supported-class-operations]. Let $\theta_c:A_B\to Rz_c^!W_c$ be its adjunct, as in [def-pur-affine-space-thom-map]. Let $u_r:W_r\to Rs_r^!W_{r+1}$ be the adjunct of
$$s_{r*}W_r\xrightarrow{\sim}s_{r*}A_{X_r}\otimes q_r^*W_r\xrightarrow{c_{s_r,A}\otimes1}W_{r+1},$$
with the canonical proper projection and twist identifications [lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula]. With $d_r:Rz_{r+1}^!\xrightarrow{\sim}Rz_r^!Rs_r^!$ conjugate to compact-support composition, the actual maps satisfy
$$C_0=1,\quad\theta_0=1,\qquad\theta_{r+1}=d_r^{-1}\circ Rz_r^!(u_r)\circ\theta_r.$$
More explicitly, $C_{r+1}$ is exactly
$$z_{r+1,*}A_B=s_{r*}z_{r*}A_B\xrightarrow{s_{r*}C_r}s_{r*}W_r\xrightarrow{\sim}s_{r*}A_{X_r}\otimes q_r^*W_r\xrightarrow{c_{s_r,A}\otimes1}W_{r+1}.$$
These are identities in the derived categories, with the same projection and composition identifications on both sides; no relative supported Kunneth isomorphism is asserted.

For any $g:B'\to B$ between the stated bases, put $g_c:X'_c\to X_c$, where $X'_c=\mathbf A^c_{B'}$. The canonical closed direct-image and Tate pullback identifications carry $g_c^*C_c$ to $C'_c$. If $\mathrm{Ex}^!_z:g^*Rz_c^!\to Rz_c'^!g_c^*$ is the mate of this closed direct-image exchange, then
$$\mathrm{Ex}^!_z(W_c)\circ g^*\theta_c=\theta'_c,$$
where $g^*A_B=A_{B'}$. This is the specified exceptional base-change mate, without a flatness hypothesis on $g$. The same formulas hold for the ordinary etale witnesses and are preserved by the exact monoidal site comparison. The products and these identities are independent of the annihilating Kummer exponent; exchanging coordinate factors has sign $(-1)^{2\cdot2}=1$.

proof.text: Now let $g:B'\to B$ be arbitrary as in the statement. Under $g_c:X'_c\to X_c$ every coordinate divisor pulls back to its namesake and remains Cartier by the coordinate polynomial calculation (multiplication by a coordinate shifts coefficients injectively, even after killing any other coordinates), even when $g$ is not flat. Cartier naturality carries each pulled-back factor to the corresponding primed factor; the supported cup pullback law carries their ordered product to the primed ordered product. The normalized closed-constant exchanges preserve coefficient restrictions and composition, so their total-intersection source comparison is the same $g_c^*z_{c*}A_B=z'_{c*}A_{B'}$ used in the statement. Hence $g_c^*C_c=C'_c$ with precisely those source, shift and Tate comparisons.

proof.text:
For the exceptional base-change identity, let $e:z'_{c*}g^*\xrightarrow{\sim}g_c^*z_{c*}$ denote the inverse of the specified closed direct-image exchange. The defining transpose of its mate $\mathrm{Ex}^!_z$ is $g_c^*\varepsilon_z\circ e$. The transpose under $z'_{c*}\dashv Rz_c'^!$ of $\mathrm{Ex}^!_z(W_c)\circ g^*\theta_c$ is consequently
$$g_c^*\varepsilon_z(W_c)\circ e_{Rz_c^!W_c}\circ z'_{c*}g^*\theta_c
=g_c^*C_c\circ e_{A_B}=C'_c.$$
The first equality is naturality of $e$ and the formula $C_c=\varepsilon_z z_{c*}\theta_c$; the second is Step 7. Bijectivity of the adjunction Hom map gives $\mathrm{Ex}^!_z(W_c)\circ g^*\theta_c=\theta'_c$. This proves an equality of mates and does not assume that exceptional base change is invertible.

proof.text: For the implemented ordinary-witness interface, first unfold ordinaryWitness and apply Equiv.apply_symm_apply to the bounded-below comparison Hom bijection. This proves ordinaryWitness_compare with exactly its specified endpoint identifications. For coordinate_section_product_ordinary, unpack the four pro-etale recursion equalities and rewrite each one inside ordinaryWitness, after introducing its arbitrary endpoint presentation. For coordinate_section_product_ordinary_baseChange, do the same with the two pro-etale base-change equalities. For coordinate_section_product_ordinary_invariance, rewrite the pro-etale permutation and exponent equalities inside every witness. These are congruence arguments on the literal witness function, so no further comparison theorem for projection, cup or exceptional functors is needed at this step. The underlying pro-etale recursion, base-change, permutation and exponent statements retain the outstanding calculations in Steps 1--8 and 10.

proof.text: Cartier naturality includes independence of the annihilating Kummer exponent for each factor, so replacing an exponent in the ordered tensor product replaces no morphism; applying the same Hom bijections replaces no adjunct either. Interchanging adjacent coordinate factors uses the supported cup symmetry with $a=b=2$, whose sign is $(-1)^{2\cdot2}=1$. Its support interchange is the unique identification of the same total coordinate zero scheme, and its target interchange is the normalized Tate multiplication. Adjacent transpositions give all coordinate permutations. These statements also persist under the site comparison of Step 9.
